findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a person runs /clear after the pane has shown rows, and the new session's first Forge read fails. The context is created once in register and is never cleared on session end, so refresh retains the old answer and view shows its rows and age. This is new evidence beyond the ruling about deleting the stored copy: Claude Code's [version-pinned hook types](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/v2.1.322/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L3475-L3480) say session.start does not fire after /clear, and the process continues under the new session. The owner-approved Done-when is: In the /forge pane, a new session whose first read fails shows only "Forge did not answer.", and each decision row shows its heading and each plain test run row opens an output file.
findings.title: Not done: New sessions retain earlier rows after /clear

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - run forge test --pytest on the default branch when no Python tests are selected but the configured command also runs a check such as mypy. fasttest.py:799-802 executes that check and returns before this log is created, so the visible test row has no output path. A queued test row also has no path while machine.join waits. Separately, even for the new log path, register.ts:151-155 refuses to read a file over 1 MiB, so a verbose test run displays 'This run has no output to show.' once its log crosses that size.
findings.title: Not done: Some plain test rows still have no usable output

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a fix and a decision use the same short name, and the decision is read from that fix's checkout. machine.py:242-249 loads the fix state for the read target; _title then takes its why at line 209 and skips this decision resolver because title is already set. The pane consequently displays the fix's description instead of the decision heading, although story.py:924-933 reads the decision file.
findings.title: Not done: A decision read can show a fix's title

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a new session starts through /clear in an existing Claude Code process. This test launches a fresh claude -p process for every pane() call, while the native pane test seeds a store before a single session start. Neither exercises a transition that retains the loaded mod's memory, so both pass while the previous session's rows reappear after /clear. The real-session helper also skips when the plugin fails to load instead of failing the proof.
findings.title: Gate: test_2_real_lane_rows_reach_the_real_pane_and_a_new_session_with_no_forge_shows_none_of_them

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a plain test produces more than 1 MiB of output. The named decision test checks the lanes JSON, and this output test checks the JSON path and reads the file directly; neither opens the actual pane row. The pane button test instead supplies a small fake file, while the real Claude test uses the non-interactive text reply. These proofs therefore pass when the real Open output pane rejects the large file and shows no output. Exercise the decision and output behavior through the pane with real Forge-produced data.
findings.title: Gate: decision heading and plain test output pane proofs

why: The pane shows the previous session's rows with their age when a new session's first read fails, shows a decision by its file name, and has no output to open for a plain test run.
